features.quote: The guiding principle throughout was *keep it minimal* — enough surface to keep a coding agent in a loop and observe it, nothing more
features.justification_quote: enough surface to keep a coding agent in a loop and observe it, nothing more
short enough to bound cost and to make "ran out of steps" a meaningful distinct outcome

features.quote: shells out to `pytest` with a 30s timeout and truncates output to 4 KB
features.justification_quote: The timeout stops infinite loops ... truncation keeps transcripts and token costs bounded

features.quote: a plain message with no tool call ends the episode (treated as a stop/handoff)
features.justification_quote: Mirrors how an agent harness typically detects "the model is done / has stopped acting"

features.quote: severity-triggered ... `SEVERITY_THRESHOLD = 1` — printed as a pass/flag check
features.justification_quote: placeholders meant to be tuned to your platform's risk tolerance

features.quote: Authorization gate + attribution. `run_battery.py` refuses to run without `--authorized`
features.justification_quote: This keeps runs attributable to a model the operator is cleared to test

features.quote: I built it fully, but pointed it honestly at the hardening use case rather than leaving it as a generic break-any-model engine
features.justification_quote: The harness is genuinely dual-use ... works as an attack harness against someone else's

features.quote: A cross-model comparison ranking ... was intentionally *not* built
features.justification_quote: while not quietly producing a turnkey "make any model fall apart" tool
